claim: Listers hear persons aggrieved by their appraisals on or before May 20 (from day to day thereafter); such hearings are not held later than June 2.
A person aggrieved by the listers' final decision may appeal in writing to the board of civil authority within 14 days after the date of notice, by lodging the appeal with the town clerk.
The town clerk calls a board of civil authority meeting to hear appeals not later than 14 days after the last date allowed for notice of appeal.

Appeal to either the Director of Property Valuation and Review or the Superior Court is commenced by filing a notice of appeal under V.R.C.P. 74 within 30 days after entry of the board of civil authority's decision.

A homestead is the principal dwelling and parcel of land surrounding the dwelling, owned and occupied by the resident as the person's domicile.

Property is nonhomestead if it is leased for more than 182 days of the calendar year, used exclusively for commercial (including rental) purposes, or used as a second home, camp, vacation or summer cottage.
Homestead owners must file a homestead declaration annually on or before the due date for the Vermont income tax return, without extension, declaring the homestead as of (or expected as of) April 1.
If an owner fails to declare a homestead, the Commissioner notifies the municipality, which issues a corrected tax bill that may include a penalty of up to 3% of the education tax.
Failure to file the declaration by the deadline means the property is classified nonhomestead and taxed at the higher rate.

Foreclosure is a court action, brought in the Superior Court Civil Division in the county where the land lies; proceedings are before the judge alone, without a jury.
The plaintiff files a copy of the complaint in the town clerk's office in each town where the property lies.
If the decree forecloses redemption without sale (strict foreclosure), redemption time is six months from the decree unless a shorter time is ordered or agreed.
Judicial sale foreclosure may be ordered on motion or at the court's discretion even if the mortgage has no sale provision.

For farmland or an owner-occupied principal residence, redemption period under a judicial sale decree is six months from the decree unless shortened; no sale of an owner-occupied dwelling may occur within seven months of service of the complaint unless shortened or agreed.
A deficiency judgment may be requested in the complaint, and must be requested before the confirmation order issues.
Real estate levied on execution is sold at public auction by the officer to the highest bidder, on the property or at a public place in the town where it lies.
The officer gives the debtor at least 60 days' written notice of the time and place of sale, by hand delivery or registered/certified mail.
The sale must also be advertised for three successive weeks before the sale in a newspaper published in the county where the land lies (or an adjoining county).
Foreclosure judicial sales: notice published once in each of three successive weeks, the first at least 21 days before sale; mailed notice at least 30 days before sale.

Small estate procedure is available if the decedent owned no real estate other than a timeshare and the estate is worth less than $45,000; filed in the Probate Division in the county where the decedent lived.
A small estate under 14 V.S.A. § 1901 has fair market value of not more than $45,000 and consists entirely of personal property (a time-share estate may be included).
To sell estate real estate, the fiduciary files a Motion for License to Sell or Convey Real Estate with the Probate Division.

The Probate Division may license the executor or administrator to sell real estate at public or private sale; a certified copy of the license is recorded where a deed would be recorded; if the will expressly confers power of sale, a license issues without notice or hearing, except for a dwelling in which a surviving spouse, heir, devisee or legatee resides.
Notice to Creditors must be published within 30 days of appointment; creditors have 4 months from publication to file claims.

The owner, lienholder or mortgagee may redeem within one year from the day of sale by paying the sale price plus interest at 1% per month or fraction thereof.
The collector must send notice to the delinquent taxpayer by certified mail between 90 and 120 days before the redemption period ends.
If not redeemed, the collector executes a deed to the purchaser conveying title against the person for whose tax it was sold.
Termination for nonpayment of rent: actual notice of a termination date at least 14 days after notice.
Termination for breach of a material term: actual notice at least 30 days before termination date; for criminal/drug/violence threatening other residents, at least 14 days.
If a tenant stays after termination without consent, the landlord may bring an action for possession under 12 V.S.A. ch. 169.
A defendant may cure a nonpayment ejectment by paying all rent due, interest and costs before the writ is executed, but not more than once in 12 months.
A writ of possession directs the sheriff to put the plaintiff in possession not earlier than 14 days after service (general rule).
